steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
Interoperability
- higher-layer services improve sync and latency: map AVB Stream ID to internal stream IDs, internal timestamps from gPTP master clock

### IEEE 1733
- IEEE Std 1733-2011: Layer 3 protocol profile for RTP applications, RTCP payload format
- Stream ID from SRP -> RTP Synchronization source identifier (SSRC)
- RTP presentation timestamps correlated with 802.1AS gPTP master clock

### AES67
- standard RTP over UDP/IP + IEEE 1588 PTPv2 for timing
- AVB/TSN interop by linking IEEE 802.1AS timing info to AES67 PTPv2 payload data
- demoed with AVB interop at InfoComm 2016

### Milan
- 2018, Avnu Alliance, Milan initiative: AVB device interoperability, certification and testing
- media clocking: AVTP CRF (Clock Reference Format); 48 kHz (optional 96 and 192 kHz)
- stream format: AVTP IEC 61883-6 32-bit Standard AAF, 1-8 channels per stream (optional 24-/32-bit High Capacity Format, 56 and 64 channels)
- redundancy: two independent logical networks per endpoint, seamless switchover

### DetNet
- IETF DetNet Working Group: deterministic data paths, bounds on latency, loss, jitter (packet delay variation), high reliability
- over Layer 2 bridged and Layer 3 routed segments; rely on AVB/TSN switch interop when possible
- application: professional A/V - music and film production, broadcast, cinema, live sound, large venues (stadiums, halls, conference centers, theme parks, airports, train terminals, etc.) for public addressing, media streaming, emergency announcement
- goal: geographically distributed campus/enterprise Intranet, bounded low latency (10-15 ms)
- single network for A/V + IT traffic; Layer 3 routing over AVB QoS networks to share content between Layer 2 AVB segments; IntServ and DiffServ integration with AVB
- unused reserved bandwidth released for best-effort traffic
- plug-and-play top to bottom: less manual setup/administration, quick changes of devices and topology
- large-scale example: ESPN SportsCenter "Digital Center 2", multiple studios, many miles of fiber, ten Tbit/s, a hundred thousand simultaneous signals
- no standards-based way to interconnect AVB segments -> custom software-defined networking router

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Higher-layer services can make synchronisation and latency of media transmission better. They do this by mapping the AVB Stream ID to their own internal stream identifiers, and by basing their internal timestamps on the gPTP master clock.

### IEEE 1733

IEEE Std 1733-2011 defines a Layer 3 protocol profile for applications using the Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP), with a RTCP payload format. It assigns the Stream ID from SRP to the Synchronization source identifier (SSRC) of RTP, and it correlates the RTP timestamps for presentation time with the 802.1AS gPTP master clock.

### AES67

AES67 is based on standard RTP over UDP/IP, and it uses IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTPv2) for timing. Interoperability with AVB/TSN can be done by linking the IEEE 802.1AS timing information to the AES67 PTPv2 payload data.

An AES67 implementation with AVB interoperability was demoed at InfoComm 2016.

### Milan
- 2018, Avnu Alliance, Milan initiative: AVB interoperability, certification and testing
- AVTP CRF clocking; 48 kHz (optional 96 and 192 kHz)
- AVTP IEC 61883-6 32-bit Standard AAF, 1-8 channels per stream (optional 24-/32-bit High Capacity Format, 56 and 64 channels)
- redundancy: two independent logical networks per endpoint, seamless switchover

### DetNet
- IETF DetNet WG: deterministic paths, bounded latency, loss, jitter, high reliability; Layer 2 + Layer 3, AVB/TSN interop when possible
- pro A/V applications: music and film production, broadcast, cinema, live sound, large venues (stadiums, halls, conference centers, theme parks, airports, train terminals, etc.); public addressing, media streaming, emergency announcement
- goal: distributed campus/enterprise Intranet, bounded low latency (10-15 ms)
- one network for A/V and IT; Layer 3 routing over AVB QoS to share between Layer 2 AVB segments; IntServ/DiffServ integration
- unused reserved bandwidth -> best-effort traffic
- plug-and-play top to bottom
- ESPN SportsCenter "Digital Center 2": many studios, miles of fiber, ten Tbit/s, a hundred thousand signals; custom software-defined networking router since no standard way to interconnect AVB segments

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Higher-layer services can make synchronisation and latency of media transmission better. They do this by mapping the AVB Stream ID to their own internal stream identifiers, and by basing their internal timestamps on the gPTP master clock.

### IEEE 1733

IEEE Std 1733-2011 defines a Layer 3 protocol profile for applications using the Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP), with a RTCP payload format. It assigns the Stream ID from SRP to the Synchronization source identifier (SSRC) of RTP, and it correlates the RTP timestamps for presentation time with the 802.1AS gPTP master clock.

### AES67

AES67 is based on standard RTP over UDP/IP, and it uses IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTPv2) for timing. Interoperability with AVB/TSN can be done by linking the IEEE 802.1AS timing information to the AES67 PTPv2 payload data.

An AES67 implementation with AVB interoperability was demoed at InfoComm 2016.

### Milan

The Avnu Alliance announced the Milan initiative in 2018. Its purpose is to promote interoperability of AVB devices and to provide product certification and testing.

The specification requires that media clocking is based on the AVTP CRF (Clock Reference Format), with a sample rate of 48 kHz, and optionally 96 and 192 kHz. The audio stream format is based on the AVTP IEC 61883-6 32-bit Standard AAF Audio Format, with 1 to 8 audio channels per stream, and optionally there is a 24- and 32-bit High Capacity Format with 56 and 64 channels. For redundancy every endpoint has two independent logical networks and there is a seamless switchover mechanism.

### DetNet

The IETF Deterministic Networking (DetNet) Working Group is working on defining deterministic data paths that have bounds on latency, loss and packet delay variation (jitter), and that have high reliability. DetNet shall work over both Layer 2 bridged segments and Layer 3 routed segments, and it will rely on interoperability with AVB/TSN switches where it is possible.

Professional audio/video is one of the possible applications of DetNet. This includes music and film production, broadcast, cinema, live sound, and also systems in large venues (stadiums, halls, conference centers, theme parks, airports, train terminals, etc.) for public addressing, media streaming and emergency announcement. The goal that is stated is to make possible a geographically distributed Intranet, campus- or enterprise-wide, for content delivery with bounded low latency (10-15 ms). One single network shall carry both A/V and IT traffic. There will be Layer 3 routing on top of AVB QoS networks so content can be shared between Layer 2 AVB segments, and IntServ and DiffServ integration with AVB where it is possible. Reserved bandwidth that is not used shall be released for best-effort traffic. The protocol stack shall be Plug-and-play from top to bottom, so there is less manual setup and administration and network devices and network topology can be changed quickly.

Large-scale AVB networks can be very big. For example the ESPN SportsCenter "Digital Center 2" broadcast facility hosts multiple individual studios, has many miles of fiber and has ten Tbit/s of bandwidth for a hundred thousand signals that are transmitted at the same time. Because there is no standards-based solution to interconnect the individual AVB segments, a custom software-defined networking router is needed.
